nyc-cb-notice.notes: Send at least 30 days before the SLA will process the application. The recipient is the community board for the premises, so the destination varies by board. Example: Manhattan CB1 takes the notice by e-mail as a PDF at onjames@cb.nyc.gov. For an e-mailed notice, the board must e-mail the SLA itself with the subject 'E-mail proof of acceptance from community board/municipality'; a sent-folder copy or read receipt is not accepted. Keep the certified-mail or delivery proof: the SLA application requires 'A COPY OF THE COMPLETED STANDARDIZED FORM AND PROOF OF DELIVERY'. Two revisions are in circulation (rev-10/23/25 in the packet, rev-04/2/26 on the standalone page): use the standalone page's. The page text was garbled, so the field order above is a reconstruction; check it against the PDF. Many boards also require their own questionnaire.

ny-sla-rw.notes: The library calls this 'RW 341'; no form with that number was found. The current form is the generic On-Premises Retail License application, with Restaurant Wine chosen through the NYBE Application Wizard. Fill it in through NYBE, then print it and mail it to the Philadelphia lockbox. The instructions don't say whether e-signatures are accepted; principals sign under penalty of perjury. Fees depend on county and beverage type (SLA retail fee schedule); the wizard cover sheet states the amount due. The license runs 2 years. The 'Notice to be Posted' must go up at the premises within 10 days of filing. The packet carries several revision stamps (rev-01/22/25 application, rev-12/19/25 checklist and method of operation). Only the first 40 lines are mapped; the packet also includes personal questionnaires and more.

cc-business-license.notes: For unincorporated Clark County only. Fee: $45 non-refundable application fee plus the category's license fee. Submit within 30 days of opening, after all construction is complete. The paper form must be filled in BLACK INK and mailed (tracked mail recommended). In person by appointment only (702-455-0174). The checklist gives the mail address as 'P.O. Box 551810, Las Vegas, NV 89155-1810', the guide page uses the street form above; both are BOX 551810. Fields after #40 on the form (owned/leased, activity, start date, signature) come from the summary's description, not printed labels, so check them against the PDF. Most licenses are issued within 45 days.

chi-sanitation.notes: The CDPH page says to pass an approved course; ANSI CFPM holders may apply for reciprocity. Processing goes through Kennedy-King College (City Colleges of Chicago), not a chicago.gov portal, so the library's 'online' method is really e-mail, mail or in person. E-mail: one combined PDF, subject line '<First Last> FSSM Application'; payment by card through a link sent after approval. Mail: money order payable to Kennedy-King College. In person: 6343 S Halsted, W142. Signature is set to 'wet' because the scanned application must be signed and no e-signature is mentioned. Fee $52; 4 to 6 weeks. This is a personal credential: the filer is the individual. ccc.edu is a public city college acting for CDPH, not a city .gov domain.

chi-license.notes: Apply online through 'Chicago Business Direct' (host not shown on the pages read) or in person at the Small Business Center, City Hall, 121 N. LaSalle St., Room 800 (312-744-6249; businesslicense@cityofchicago.org is for help, not filing). In-person applicants complete a Business Information Sheet pre-application. The premises must pass a CDPH health inspection before the license is issued. Two fee tables conflict. Current BACP page: $660 (0-1,000 sq ft), $940 (1,001-2,500), $1,110 (2,501-4,500), $1,320 (4,501-10,000), $1,650 (over 10,000). The older guide: $660 / $880 / $1,100. Use the BACP page. 2-year term. Unpaid City debt must be cleared before the license is issued.
